one_line: Compass gives agents bounded, auditable access to selected personal context.
what_it_does: Local-first notes, tasks, bookmarks, snippets, spaces, and permissioned Context Packs exposed through typed WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides a structured, permission-aware shared state surface with live UI updates, audit entries, and explicit write revocation; general UI-driving agents would be materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Ten typed tools cover context retrieval, search, writes, task completion, linking, and pack creation.
Permission changes rebuild the registry and handlers repeat permission and Pack checks.
Agent writes appear live with readable audit entries and Undo.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent local-first workflow and includes frame-sheet evidence of search and a visible task change, though the supplied visual evidence is low-resolution and no transcript is available.
execution_evidence: React/TypeScript/Vite interface with Dexie IndexedDB persistence and Zod validation is described.
Frame sheet shows agent search/result and a tool call associated with a persistent visible task.
Seeded Project Atlas flow specifies search, create, disable writes, confirm disappearance, and undo.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete privacy and control problem for people using personal agents: sharing useful context without handing over an entire workspace.
impact_evidence: Context Packs constrain Spaces, selected items, item types, and read/write switches.
The product supports tasks, references, decisions, and safe fictional seed data.
creativity_rationale: Making the context boundary a temporary, understandable, inspectable object is a strong and memorable interaction model for personal agents.
creativity_evidence: Context Pack is a first-class permission boundary rather than a broad authorization screen.
Human-visible undo and audit entries extend the concept beyond basic CRUD.
usability_note: Clear bounded-context model and seeded workspace suggest approachable use, though visual readability is only partly demonstrated.
red_flags: No video or transcript; frame sheets are low resolution and do not independently show exact tool mechanics.
standouts: Permission-aware shared state with immediate registry changes and reversible agent writes.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-specific privacy/control thesis with coherent evidence and meaningful product value.

one_line: Stamped lets an agent parse a resume, match jobs, and draft tailored cover letters.
what_it_does: A job application portal using three WebMCP tools backed by shared Blazor/C# logic, while preserving manual control of application submission.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools make chained resume parsing, job matching, and drafting more reliable than UI automation, but the same workflow remains possible with a general agent with friction.
leverage_evidence: Three tools expose parseResume, matchJobs, and draftCoverLetter.
Tool execution bridges to the same backend and database as the UI.
There is deliberately no agent application-submission tool.
execution_rationale: The described chain is coherent and claims end-to-end testing, but there are no frame sheets or video evidence and the packet text is incomplete.
execution_evidence: Blazor Server backend, JS interop, and shared C# logic are specified.
Accomplishment claims a working end-to-end WebMCP tool chain.
Devpost packaging screenshot is the only visual surface supplied.
impact_rationale: Job seekers have a clear tedious workflow and the product directly reduces resume comparison and generic-letter effort while retaining the consequential apply decision.
impact_evidence: Resume parsing, ranked openings, reasoning, and match-specific cover letters address a concrete job-search burden.
Manual-only submission preserves user agency.
creativity_rationale: A sensible agent-assisted job-search workflow with a good safety boundary, but the core category and interaction are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Explicit separation between agent preparation and manual application is thoughtful.
Backend-backed callable tool chain is a practical synthesis rather than a novel concept.
usability_note: The staged pipeline should be understandable, though usability is not directly demonstrated beyond packaging.
red_flags: No submitted video frames or transcript; end-to-end claims are weakly evidenced.
standouts: Safety-conscious omission of submitApplication from the agent surface.
advance_reason: Clear audience and useful workflow; advance despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: Islanding lets an agent explore constrained power-restoration plans while a human approves the exact switching sequence.
what_it_does: A seeded electrical-grid digital twin exposes topology, simulation, preview, stale-state invalidation, and approval-bound execution through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Semantic, typed access to topology, constraints, deterministic simulation, state versions, and exact approval hashes is central; screen-driving cannot comparably provide safe reliable operation.
leverage_evidence: Nine tools read incident/topology state, simulate plans, compare tradeoffs, and prepare a preview.
Human edits increment state version and invalidate drafts and approvals.
Execution is bound to current draft hash/version and cannot be approved by the agent.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a deeply coherent seeded workflow with visible frame evidence of the operational interface and receipt, though no transcript or observed live run is included.
execution_evidence: Specific storm scenario, reserve threshold, blocked 18% plan, valid 27% plan, and receipt are described.
Frame sheets show the grid/operator workflow and result states.
Human approval and stale-state handling are integrated into the central flow.
impact_rationale: For grid operators and critical-infrastructure planning, preventing unsafe switching while accelerating restoration is a high-value, credible use case even as a synthetic digital twin.
impact_evidence: Hospital, shelter, and water restoration are explicit outcomes.
Reserve constraints and fault interlocks model consequential operational requirements.
creativity_rationale: It uses WebMCP as a semantic safety/control plane for a professional digital twin, with human priorities and agent exploration cleanly divided.
creativity_evidence: Exact-sequence approval invalidated by human state changes is an unusually strong interaction model.
The project demonstrates consequences rather than merely exposing CRUD tools.
usability_note: Operator-oriented language and explicit gates help, though the domain is inherently specialized.
red_flags: Synthetic scenario; no transcript and agent invocation is not directly visible in the frame sheets.
standouts: State-versioned approval and semantic safety boundary are exceptionally well matched to WebMCP.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and ambitious, safety-conscious domain application.

one_line: Lyrashield scans WebMCP definitions for risky contracts and supports reviewed in-memory rewrites.
what_it_does: A browser-local assurance lab parses tool source, runs deterministic controls, previews a remediation diff, applies it in memory, and reruns checks.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the object being analyzed and the agent-assisted review loop operates on structured tool contracts; typed surfaces materially improve assurance compared with generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Fourteen browser-local controls inspect descriptions, input contracts, permissions, and implementations.
Rewrite preview changes exposedTo and reruns the assurance checks.
Human review controls whether the in-memory change is applied.
execution_rationale: The packet provides unusually concrete control counts, findings, remediation, and many screenshots, indicating a coherent release-assurance workflow.
execution_evidence: Unsafe delete_user sample yields seven DETECTED controls.
WEBMCP-03 rewrite and rerun changes exposure control to NO FINDING.
Twelve gallery images cover lab, scans, launch readiness, and review states.
impact_rationale: Developers shipping browser-agent tools face real risks from mismatched contracts and permissions; local pre-release checks directly address that need.
impact_evidence: The sample demonstrates a readOnlyHint/DELETE/exposedTo disagreement.
No account or API key is required, lowering trial friction.
creativity_rationale: Treating WebMCP tool definitions as auditable release artifacts with deterministic controls and agent-assisted remediation is a fresh, focused concept.
creativity_evidence: Browser-local security lab combines static assurance, diff review, and rerun verification.
The workflow makes source stay local and keeps application under human review.
usability_note: Concrete controls, evidence, and remediation guidance suggest strong developer usability.
red_flags: No video/transcript; claims of agent-assisted action are not directly shown in submitted frame sheets.
standouts: Specific, reproducible unsafe sample and remediation loop.
advance_reason: Strong execution and a directly relevant, differentiated WebMCP security workflow.

one_line: Quorum lets human and agent participants negotiate meeting times in one shared session.
what_it_does: A scheduler exposes event state, joining, voting, counter-proposals, and ranking as WebMCP tools with a visible shared log and human organizer approval.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables agents to participate as first-class, stateful negotiators alongside humans, with typed chaining and shared visibility; UI-driving agents would be unreliable for this interaction.
leverage_evidence: Seven tools support read state, join, vote with reasons, counter-propose, and rank.
Actions land in a shared log tagged HUMAN or AGENT.
Only the human organizer can accept or lock the final time.
execution_rationale: The central negotiation model is coherent and frame sheets provide product-state evidence, but no transcript and no public repository reduce verification.
execution_evidence: Packet describes a four-tool first-try chain from read state through winner report.
Frame sheets show scheduler and negotiation-log states.
Human and agent actions are explicitly modeled as shared session events.
impact_rationale: Scheduling across people with conflicting constraints is common and the product offers credible relief while retaining organizer control.
impact_evidence: Candidate times and yes/maybe/no votes address real coordination friction.
Agents can represent unavailable participants without hiding actions.
creativity_rationale: Mixed human-agent negotiation, rather than agent-only scheduling, is a notably fresh interaction model with visible trust mechanisms.
creativity_evidence: Agents are equal participants in the live session.
Reasoned votes and counter-proposals create an explicit negotiation loop.
usability_note: Familiar poll-like UI plus visible log should make the mixed-participant model legible.
red_flags: No public repository and repo_archived field is blank; eligibility evidence is incomplete.
standouts: Shared human/agent negotiation with complete mutual visibility.
advance_reason: Distinctive and valuable WebMCP-native collaboration model; eligibility needs verification.

one_line: Incident Relay lets agents investigate and stage SRE mitigations behind an operator approval gate.
what_it_does: A client-side incident workbench exposes telemetry, diagnostics, rollback staging/execution, and postmortem drafting with replay protection.
leverage_rationale: Structured incident state and guarded staged execution make WebMCP central to safe agent participation in operational response; generic UI automation cannot reliably preserve the approval boundary.
leverage_evidence: Seven typed tools cover detect-to-recover investigation and mitigation flow.
stage_mitigation prepares a proposal but there is no approval tool.
Execution revalidates phase, mitigation IDs, approval source, and replay conditions.
execution_rationale: The packet specifies a complete, coherent incident lifecycle with concrete metrics and frame-sheet support, though invocation details are not directly observable.
execution_evidence: Specific regression metrics, rollback plan, blast radius, and recovery metrics are given.
Frame sheets show incident dashboard, evidence, approval, and recovery states.
Agent-drafted postmortem and audit-oriented controls complete the workflow.
impact_rationale: SRE teams have a clear high-stakes need for faster investigation without delegating unsafe production execution; the simulated checkout incident maps directly to that need.
impact_evidence: The product combines service health, SLO charts, alerts, logs, diffs, diagnostics, and timeline.
Explicit operator approval and replay protection reduce operational risk.
creativity_rationale: The product turns the investigate-versus-execute accountability boundary into a first-class interaction rather than a prompt instruction.
creativity_evidence: No approval tool and UI-only approval are deliberate architecture choices.
Staged exact rollback plus revalidation is a memorable agent-native SRE pattern.
usability_note: Rich operational context is useful for experts, though density may raise onboarding cost.
red_flags: Simulated incident and no transcript; frame sheets do not directly prove agent calls.
standouts: Strong approval boundary with replay protection and exact mitigation validation.
advance_reason: High-impact, high-leverage workflow with strong claimed completeness.

one_line: CLOTHO turns a wardrobe and calendar into agent-planned, human-approved outfit strategies.
what_it_does: A local-first wardrobe planner lets agents search, constrain, generate, recolor, schedule, remember, import, and export outfits around weather and taste.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools expose many interdependent wardrobe, calendar, weather, and durable-state operations; structured constraints and human application boundaries provide a meaningful advantage over UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Agent plans 21 calendar moments across three strategies from one constrained request.
Results include scores, reasons, weather context, conflicts, and repetition tradeoffs.
Nothing reaches the durable calendar until a person selects and explicitly applies it.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a polished end-to-end planning concept and six gallery images cover wardrobe and planning states, though there is no transcript.
execution_evidence: Explicit seven-day, three-times-per-day scenario yields three visible strategies.
Gallery evidence covers product views and outfit planning.
Import/export, scheduling, history, and human apply boundary indicate scope completeness.
impact_rationale: People managing clothing, weather, events, and repetition constraints have a real recurring planning burden; the product addresses it with owned items and calendar context.
impact_evidence: The workflow coordinates wardrobe inventory, calendar, weather, taste, and recent wear.
Human choice remains final for durable scheduling.
creativity_rationale: The wardrobe-calendar thread and multi-strategy planning interaction are distinctive, playful, and pursued with unusually rich constraints for a hackathon.
creativity_evidence: Named concept connects actual catalog items to future moments and wear history.
Three strategy outputs expose tradeoffs instead of returning one opaque recommendation.
usability_note: Concrete request format, visible strategies, and explicit apply step support understandable use.
red_flags: Weather/calendar integrations and generation depth are claimed but not fully independently observable.
standouts: Human-approved, constraint-rich outfit strategies spanning 21 calendar moments.
advance_reason: Memorable concept with strong evidence of a coherent, agent-native planning workflow.

one_line: CanvasMind lets agents read floor plans and audit wheelchair accessibility continuously.
what_it_does: A dependency-free room planner checks reachability, doorway clear zones, overlaps, and exports an image stamped with a human-readable verdict.
leverage_rationale: Structured geometry and continuous accessibility calculations are far more precise and repeatable through tools than general agents visually driving a canvas.
leverage_evidence: Checks continuous 90cm routes from doors to every item, not only pairwise gaps.
Agent can perform the same planning/audit operations as the UI.
Export embeds the verdict as a shareable record.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a concrete algorithmic scope and frame sheets show the planner/audit presentation, but no transcript or live observed run is supplied.
execution_evidence: Specific 13m × 8m scenario reports all 31 seats reachable on a 90cm route.
Four continuous checks and human-language verdicts are described.
Vanilla JS/Canvas/WebMCP implementation is scoped to about 1,400 lines with no build step.
impact_rationale: Venue designers and accessibility auditors have a concrete safety and inclusion problem that visual inspection and manual route tracing routinely miss.
impact_evidence: The tool identifies unreachable seats and doorway clear-zone violations.
Exported stamped plan can become a client-facing record.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent-readable structural geometry to accessibility auditing is a strong, socially meaningful angle beyond generic floor-plan editing.
creativity_evidence: Continuous route reachability addresses a subtle failure mode pairwise checks miss.
The agent-readable floor-plan framing is concise and memorable.
usability_note: Plain-language verdicts and direct manipulation support accessibility-audit workflows, though canvas editing can be demanding.
red_flags: Repo-archived field is blank; frame sheets do not clearly expose exact agent invocation.
standouts: Continuous route analysis produces a concrete, client-shareable accessibility verdict.
advance_reason: High credible impact and strong structured-geometry leverage; verify eligibility details.

one_line: AI Tool Scout turns a business need and budget into transparent software recommendations.
what_it_does: A browser-local scout exposes a shared recommendation engine to humans and agents, with budget gates, archive redirects, cards, JSON, and flight recording.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives agents a direct structured recommendation call and synchronized page result, but the underlying form and engine still work in plain Chrome, so the delta is meaningful rather than transformative.
leverage_evidence: ChatGPT calls find_ai_tools via WebMCP and results land in chat and on the page.
The same engine serves human and agent requests.
Budget gate and JSON/card dual presentation support agent and human consumption.
execution_rationale: Multiple screenshots show a coherent scout, budget fallback, shared engine, and flight recorder, but there are no video frames/transcript and the packet text is incomplete.
execution_evidence: Gallery includes WebMCP call, plain Chrome fallback, recommendation cards, budget gate, and flight recorder.
The packet describes browser-local query privacy and an archive redirect.
Three vetted tools and lowest-known-price fallback form a complete stated flow.
impact_rationale: Small businesses and teams choosing AI software face a real opaque, budget-constrained comparison problem; transparent recommendations and fallback pricing address it directly.
impact_evidence: Task description plus budget yields three vetted tools.
Budget gate answers when nothing fits rather than silently failing.
creativity_rationale: The combination of budget-aware recommendations, synchronized agent/human output, and privacy-preserving flight recording is a fresh synthesis of a familiar scout category.
creativity_evidence: Agent Flight Recorder captures a four-step trace while keeping query text local.
Plain-Chrome fallback makes the WebMCP delta legible.
usability_note: Task-plus-budget input, cards for humans, and JSON for agents suggest a clear dual-audience workflow.
red_flags: No video frame sheets; recommendation quality and vetting depth are not independently demonstrated.
standouts: Explicit comparison against plain Chrome and privacy-preserving agent flight recorder.
advance_reason: Clear audience/problem fit and credible shared human-agent experience, with moderate WebMCP delta.

one_line: BuildAI Command is a governed dashboard where agents run, monitor, and request approval for agent actions.
what_it_does: A single screen exposes agent listing, runs, status, and approval through the same governed backend path used by humans.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets ChatGPT operate the platform through the same governed path, including status and approval, preserving shared state and policy rather than merely clicking controls.
leverage_evidence: The same actions are exposed as tools and used by humans through the platform.
Agent can list agents, start a run, check status, and approve a step.
Approvals gate sensitive actions such as sending an email.
execution_rationale: The described one-screen flow is coherent, but no video frames/transcript are provided and the packet ends before implementation details and live proof.
execution_evidence: Three panels cover Agents, Activity, and Approvals.
Claimed demo flow runs a support agent and approves an email after review.
Existing backend is said to perform the real work, but completeness is not directly evidenced.
impact_rationale: Teams operating AI workers need visibility and accountable approval for consequential actions; the dashboard directly addresses governance and monitoring.
impact_evidence: Activity monitoring and approval/rejection are first-class panels.
Human and ChatGPT use the same governed action path.
creativity_rationale: Governed agent operations in a shared dashboard are valuable and well aligned with WebMCP, though agent-control dashboards are an established category.
creativity_evidence: Approval-aware operation through the browser is a practical interaction model.
The product thesis explicitly centers memory, tools, policy, and human approval.
usability_note: Three-panel information architecture is understandable, but login and absent visual execution evidence limit assessment.
red_flags: No frame sheets or transcript; public repository is absent; packet evidence is incomplete.
Product appears to be an existing BuildAI platform adapted for the challenge, so origin and eligibility need verification.
standouts: Same governed path for human and agent approval actions.
advance_reason: Potentially strong concept, but execution and eligibility are too weakly evidenced in this packet.
